decisions.statement: A capture is filed as a page of the runtime-error page type.
A capture asks for the page filed under its fingerprint before writing anything.
A capture finding no page files a page with a count of 1.
A capture finding a page raises that page's count.
A capture finding a page moves the moment that error was last met.
A capture finding a page hands back the values the commit already has.
A capture of an error already filed lands no commit.
A capture finding a page whose count was never read writes no count.
A page is handed over as values rather than as a path and a body.
Which values reach the commit is settled by the runtime-error page type.
Nobody who met an error is named.
Nothing here decides whether an error is worth filing.
A refusal from the pages is thrown rather than swallowed.
Two captures of one error arriving together leave the count short.

definition: an error a client met, filed as a page
